advanced.title: What Are Advanced Linear Equations?
advanced.intro: Advanced linear equations are equations where the variable appears to the first power, but solving them requires multiple steps and special techniques.
advanced.discovery: Let's unlock powerful strategies for tackling complex equations! These skills are essential for physics, engineering, and real-world problem solving.

absolute.title: Absolute Value
absolute.concept: Absolute value |x| represents the distance from zero, always positive or zero.

multiStep.title: Multi-Step Equations
multiStep.intro: Multi-step equations require combining several algebraic techniques: distributing, combining like terms, and isolating the variable.

fractions.title: Equations with Fractions
fractions.intro: When equations contain fractions, multiply both sides by the LCD (Least Common Denominator) to clear the fractions!

absolute.title: Absolute Value Equations
absolute.intro: Absolute value equations have TWO possible solutions because |x| can equal a positive number in two ways.

multiStep.title: Solving Multi-Step Equations
multiStep.caption: Follow the order: Distribute → Combine → Isolate

fractions.title: Clearing Fractions
fractions.caption: Multiply by LCD to eliminate all fractions at once!

absolute.title: Solving Absolute Value Equations
absolute.caption: Split into TWO cases: positive and negative

steps.title: Order of Operations for Solving:
steps.content: 1) Distribute, 2) Combine like terms, 3) Get variables on one side, 4) Isolate the variable, 5) Check your solution!

example1.title: Example 1: Multi-Step with Distribution
example1.step3: Step 3: Combine like terms and get variables on one side

example2.title: Example 2: Equation with Fractions
example2.step1: Step 1: Find LCD of 3 and 6, which is 6. Multiply everything by 6

mistake1.title: Only Distributing to the First Term
mistake1.wrong: When distributing 4(x - 2), students might only multiply the x:
mistake1.correct: Distribute to BOTH terms inside the parentheses:
mistake1.explanation: The distributive property means multiply EVERY term inside. Think of it like handing out 4 cookies to everyone in the room—nobody gets left out!
mistake1.tip: Always count: if there are 2 terms inside, you should get 2 products after distributing.

mistake2.title: Forgetting the Second Solution in Absolute Value
mistake2.correct: Absolute value equations need BOTH cases (positive and negative):
mistake2.explanation: The absolute value of a number can equal 7 in two ways: if the number is 7 OR if it's -7. Always solve both cases!

mistake3.title: Not Multiplying All Terms by LCD
mistake3.wrong: When clearing fractions, students forget to multiply the right side:
mistake3.correct: The LCD must multiply EVERY single term, including those on the right side:
mistake3.explanation: Think of multiplying by LCD as a rule that applies to the entire equation, not just one side. Every term gets multiplied—no exceptions!

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
realWorld.intro: Advanced linear equations aren't just classroom exercises—they're problem-solving tools used by professionals every day!

app1.title: ⚗️ Chemistry & Solution Mixing
app1.description: Chemists use linear equations to calculate how to mix solutions of different concentrations.
app1.example: Example: Mixing 30% acid with 50% acid to get 40% solution uses: 0.3x + 0.5(20-x) = 0.4(20)

app2.title: 💼 Business Break-Even Analysis
app2.description: Businesses find break-even points where revenue equals costs.
app2.example: If costs are 5x + 2000 and revenue is 12x, break-even: 12x = 5x + 2000

app3.title: 🔧 Engineering & Physics
app3.description: Engineers model physical relationships using linear equations.
app3.example: Unit conversion, force calculations, equilibrium points all use these equations

warmup.title: Warm-up Problems
warmup.description: Build your confidence with these foundational problems!

exercise4.question: Solve: |x - 2| = 5. What is the SMALLER solution? Enter the value.
exercise4.explanation: Case 1: x = 7. Case 2: x = -3. The smaller solution is -3

exercise5.question: Which has infinitely many solutions?
exercise5.explanation: 3(x + 1) = 3x + 3 simplifies to 3x + 3 = 3x + 3, which is true for all x!

exercise6.question: A phone plan costs $15/month plus $0.50/min. Your bill was $30. How many minutes did you use? Enter the number.

notes.title: Tips & Strategies
notes.tip1: 📝 Always distribute FIRST before combining like terms. This prevents sign errors!
notes.tip2: 🎯 For fractions, find the LCD and multiply the ENTIRE equation by it. This eliminates all fractions in one step.
notes.tip3: 💡 After solving, always check your answer by substituting back into the original equation. This catches calculation errors!

conclusion.title: You're Now an Equation-Solving Expert! 🎉
conclusion.summary: Advanced linear equations prepare you for complex problem-solving in science, engineering, and everyday life. You've learned to handle multi-step problems, fractions, and absolute values—skills that will serve you throughout your mathematical journey!
conclusion.takeaway1: Multi-step equations: distribute, combine, isolate, solve
conclusion.takeaway2: Clear fractions by multiplying entire equation by LCD
conclusion.takeaway3: Absolute value equations have TWO solutions (check both cases)
conclusion.takeaway4: Always verify your solution in the original equation
